subject: Private observability: Splunk HEC collector + bastion egress coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ian Carter <ian.carter@acmecloud.com>; ACME Onboarding <onboard@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private observability: Splunk HEC collector + bastion egress coordination

Hi Ian / onboarding team —

Thanks for the call this week. Per our internal review, we want to confirm the proposed approach for shipping observability from the Redwood Private deployment in your VPC into ACME's Splunk HEC endpoint while respecting your no-outbound-internet policy. High level plan:

- Deploy a small Redwood forwarder container inside the customer VPC (in the same subnet as the model nodes) that buffers and forwards events.
- Use mutual TLS (mTLS) to authenticate to your Splunk HEC endpoint.
- Where direct egress is disallowed, route traffic through a customer-managed bastion / egress proxy in the subnet that has an approved tunnel to your on-prem SIEM (IPsec/VPN or PrivateLink).

Attached: collector-config-example.yaml and a simple network-egress-diagram.png showing the proposed path.

Requests for you to confirm:
1) Preferred ingestion method: Splunk HEC (TLS 8088) or on-prem Syslog/HEC over forwarded VPN?
2) If HEC, please provide the HEC host (private IP / DNS), port, and the expected CN for cert validation.
3) If a bastion is required, confirm the egress proxy host and which ports we can use between forwarder->bastion.
4) Retention / PII filtering expectations (we can apply scrubbing on the forwarder).

If it's easier we can do a 20-minute handoff call next week to walk the runbook and cert exchange.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments (3): collector-config-example.yaml (text/yaml), network-egress-diagram.png (image/png), redwood-forwarder-runbook.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ian Carter <ian.carter@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Onboarding <onboard@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability: Splunk HEC collector + bastion egress coordination

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the diagrams. A few notes from our side after running this past infra/security:

- Direct outbound to the public internet is not allowed from the VPC. We prefer one of these patterns:
  * PrivateLink from Redwood to our Splunk VPC (preferred), or
  * Forwarder -> customer bastion -> encrypted VPN to on-prem SIEM (acceptable), or
  * S3-bucket pickup is allowed for bulk transfer but not for near-real-time logs.

- If you must use HEC over TLS (8088), it will need to be over our private network via PrivateLink or the bastion. We will provide a private DNS entry (internal) if PrivateLink is used.

- Certs: we require mTLS with client cert pinning. We can generate a CSR for you to sign, or we can accept a Redwood-supplied client cert if you can pin the SHA256 thumbprint.

- Filtering: we do require PII scrubbing prior to leaving the VPC. Please include the scrub template you use (redaction rules).

Next steps from ACME:
1) Confirm which connectivity option you prefer (PrivateLink / bastion / S3).
2) If PrivateLink, share the VPC CIDR for peering checks.
3) We'll open a ticket with networking to provision the PrivateLink endpoint and a private DNS record (ETA 4 business days).

Ian
Ian Carter
Product Security, ACMEcloud

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ian Carter <ian.carter@acmecloud.com>; ACME Onboarding <onboard@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability: Splunk HEC collector + bastion egress coordination

Ian / ACME team —

Appreciate the clear constraints. Short technical responses and an implementation offer from our side: 

1) Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink is ideal for low-latency, authenticated traffic. If ACME can provision a PrivateLink endpoint on your side we'll consume it from the Redwood-managed ENI in the Private Subnet.

2) mTLS + cert pinning: Redwood can produce a CSR for your CA to sign. Alternatively we can accept ACME-supplied client certs and handle rotating them via the forwarder config. We'll include a small cert-rotation utility in the runbook.

3) PII scrubbing: our forwarder supports configurable redaction rules. Attached collector-config-example.yaml includes a sample scrub template (fields to remove or hash). We will not send raw user text fields unless you explicitly allow them.

4) Bastion mode option: if you go with a bastion, recommended configuration:
   - Forwarder -> bastion on 127.0.0.1:9443 (local bind) inside the subnet;
   - Bastion performs TLS termination and sends to ACME SIEM over the approved tunnel;
   - Bastion should run in a hardened subnet with limited inbound admin access (jump host).

Operational checklist (what we need from ACME):
- PrivateLink service name (if used) or bastion host IP/DNS
- Preferred cert delivery method (CSR or provide client cert)
- Confirmation of PII retention policy and scrub rules (we will default to 30d retention for diagnostic logs unless otherwise specified)

We can provide a short playbook (we've attached redwood-forwarder-runbook.pdf) and we're happy to do a live runbook walk. If you prefer PrivateLink, we'll need the VPC CIDR and the AWS account ID for peering checks.

Marissa will coordinate the pre-handoff call.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability: Splunk HEC collector + bastion egress coordination

Ian / team —

Thanks — here's the plan and next steps so we can lock the handoff: 

1) Connectivity choice: Please confirm PrivateLink if possible. If yes, share ACME AWS account ID and the service name; we'll start the peering checks.

2) Certs: ACME to confirm whether you will provide a client cert (preferred for pinning) or if you want Redwood to generate a CSR.

3) Network & ports: If PrivateLink, no public egress required. If bastion, open the following (internal-only) between forwarder and bastion: TCP 9443 (forwarder -> bastion), TCP 22 (admin only, bastion management).

4) Security: we'll apply the attached PII scrub template by default and will not forward fields marked as PHI unless you sign off.

5) Book time: propose a 20-min handoff on Tue 05/04 10:00 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda: cert exchange, PrivateLink checks, and quick runbook demo.

Drive runbook link and Jira: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/0ABXx-example-runbook | Jira: OBS-4521

If we don't hear back on PrivateLink by EOD Mon we'll queue bastion-mode as fallback and schedule the handoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
